mn_sandstone.blurb: Sandstone is a small town off I-35 between the Twin Cities and Duluth, and its climbing falls into three parts. Robinson Park, beside the Kettle River, has sport routes (mostly 5.10 to 5.12, with some moderates), a few boulders, and farmed ice and dry tooling. The ice park runs down rock walls left by an old mining operation, where volunteers build much of the ice with pipes and misters, so it is a winter activity. Across the river, the Eldon boulders offer sandstone bouldering from V0 up to V10. Robinson Park and Eldon can be climbed year-round, but wet sandstone is prone to breaking, so wait for it to dry after rain.

ny_nine_corner_lake.blurb: Nine Corner Lake is a bouldering area in the Southern Adirondacks of New York, set beside the lake at the end of a short forest walk from the road. Every climb is a boulder problem, and the grades lean friendly: most are V0 to V5, with a thinner spread of harder problems up to V9. The blocks are large and well shaded, and the rock is good, though some top-outs feel sketchy. Middle Earth is the main concentration of boulders, with sections such as Lookout, Fortress and Tower; Roadside Nine, The Meadows and Stonehenge are the other main zones.

az_paradise_forks.blurb: Paradise Forks is a trad crack-climbing area on the rim of Sycamore Canyon in northern Arizona, southeast of Williams and west of Flagstaff. The cliffs are columnar basalt, hard and typically well protected, set in pine forest where two arms of the canyon meet and carry seasonal waterfalls. Nearly all routes are traditional cracks, and many are reached by fixing a line from above and rappelling in; sport climbing is almost absent. Ratings are stout: grades run from about 5.8 up to 5.13, concentrated between 5.10 and 5.12. The Prow, Gold Wall, Davidson Wall and White Wall hold the most climbs.

bc_powell_river.blurb: Powell River, officially qathet now, is on the Sunshine Coast of British Columbia, and its climbing is scattered across several areas rather than a single crag. Eldred Valley is the main hub, with granite walls and multi-pitch routes that run from the middle grades up to grade VI big-wall aid. Other areas include Stillwater, Higgyland, High Five and Lois Lake Bluffs, plus Haslam Lake Boulders for bouldering. Trad is the most common style, with sport and bouldering both well represented. Sport and trad grades are mostly 5.9 to 5.11, with a fair number at 5.12, and the boulder problems stay mostly between V1 and V5.

ca_daff_area.blurb: The Daff Area is a cluster of domes and walls in Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite National Park, just off Tioga Road west of Fairview Dome. Trad is the main style, with alpine routes, some sport and a few top-rope climbs too. Daff Dome is a granite dome with multi-pitch slab and crack routes, while the Cottage Domes nearby are known for steep knob climbing on East Cottage Dome. Grades run from about 5.5 up to 5.12, most between 5.8 and 5.11 and peaking at 5.10. Daff Dome and the Cottage Domes hold the most climbing, followed by The Southern Front, mostly top-rope, and Dark Side Dome.
